1.q: וַֽ⁠יְהִי֙ בַּ⁠שָּׁנָ֣ה הָ⁠רְבִיעִ֔ת לִ⁠יהוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה
1.note: Jeremiah is using the phrase translated as **Now it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
See how you translated the similar expression in [25:1](ta:25).

1.q: הָיָ֞ה הַ⁠דָּבָ֤ר הַ⁠זֶּה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵ⁠אֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה
1.note: Jeremiah is using **this word was to Jeremiah from Yahweh** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh spoke this message to Jeremiah.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that Yahweh gave this message to Jeremiah]
See how you translated this name in [35:1](ta:35). This also occurs in verse 9.

1.q: הָיָ֞ה הַ⁠דָּבָ֤ר הַ⁠זֶּה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵ⁠אֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה
1.note: Jeremiah is speaking of himself in the third person as **Jeremiah**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this form in the first person. Alternate translation: [that this word came to me, Jeremiah, from Yahweh]

2.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **scroll** that is characterized by being used as a **book**, that is, a scroll used to write things on. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a scroll for writing a document]

Here, the term **scroll** refers to a kind of writing material made from rolled-up sheets that were made from the papyrus plant or leather. If your readers would not be familiar with what a scroll is, you could use a more general term or make a footnote that explains what a scroll is. Alternate translation: [a rolled sheet of writing material]
Yahweh is using the term **words** to represent what he said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly as in the UST.

Yahweh is using the term **days** to refer to a specific time period. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from when Josiah was reigning as king until now]

3.note: See how you translated this phrase in 12:14.
See how you translated this expression in 12:15.

3.q: אוּלַ֤י יִשְׁמְעוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה אֵ֚ת כָּל הָ֣⁠רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י חֹשֵׁ֖ב לַ⁠עֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ⁠הֶ֑ם לְמַ֣עַן יָשׁ֗וּבוּ אִ֚ישׁ מִ⁠דַּרְכּ֣⁠וֹ הָ⁠רָעָ֔ה וְ⁠סָלַחְתִּ֥י לַ⁠עֲוֺנָ֖⁠ם וּ⁠לְ⁠חַטָּאתָֽ⁠ם
3.note: Here, **so that** marks **they may turn back, a man from his evil way** as the goal or purpose of **the house of Judah will listen to all the evil that I am planning to do to them**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the way a person behaves were a **way** or path on which he walks. For **a man** to **turn back…from his evil way** means that each person should stop behaving in evil ways. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [each one of them may stop doing evil things]
See how you translated the similar expression in 16:18.

4.note: The word **Neriah** is the name of a man.

Here, **mouth** represents “what Jeremiah said aloud.” Jeremiah spoke the words and Baruch wrote them down. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. This also occurs in verses 27 and 32. Alternate translation: [as Jeremiah dictated]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:9. This also occurs in verses 6, 8, 11, and 27.

Here the pronoun **he** could: (1) refer to Yahweh, and the pronoun **him** would then refer to Jeremiah. (In verse 2 Yahweh tells Jeremiah to write on a scroll “all the words that I have spoken to you.”) Alternate translation: [that Yahweh had spoken to Jeremiah] (2) refer to Jeremiah, and the pronoun **him** would then refer to Baruch. Alternate translation: [that Jeremiah had spoken to Baruch]
See how you translated this expression in 36:2.

5.note: The expression **I am restrained** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The text does not say who was restraining Jeremiah, so if you need to state who did the action, you could use a general expression such as “someone” or “the authorities.” Alternate translation: [The authorities are restraining me]

The implication is that something was preventing Jeremiah from going to the temple himself. Most likely Jeremiah had been forbidden from entering the temple. Alternate translation: [I have been forbidden to go to the temple]
See how you translated this phrase in 17:26. This also occurs in verses 6, 8, and 10.

6.note: Jeremiah is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you shall go** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that Baruch must go in his place, since Jeremiah cannot go himself. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [And you yourself shall go in my place]

Here, **in the ears of the people** represents “where the people can hear.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. This also occurs in verses 10, 13, 14, 15, 20, and 21. This also occurs in verses 13 and 14. Alternate translation: [where the people can hear … where the people of Judah can hear] or [in the hearing of the people … in the hearing of the people of Judah]

Jeremiah is not distinguishing these people of **Judah** from other people of Judah who were not **coming from their cities**. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [all the people of Judah, that is, those who had come from their cities]

7.q: אוּלַ֞י תִּפֹּ֤ל תְּחִנָּתָ⁠ם֙ לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְ⁠יָשֻׁ֕בוּ אִ֖ישׁ מִ⁠דַּרְכּ֣⁠וֹ הָ⁠רָעָ֑ה כִּֽי גָד֤וֹל הָ⁠אַף֙ וְ⁠הַ֣⁠חֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל הָ⁠עָ֥ם הַ⁠זֶּֽה
7.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Because great is the nose and the heat that Yahweh has spoken against this people, perhaps their supplication will fall to the face of Yahweh, and they will turn back, a man from his evil way]

Jeremiah is using **their supplication will fall to the face of Yahweh** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they will humbly present their request to Yahweh.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Perhaps they will humbly present their request to Yahweh] or [Perhaps they will humbly pray for mercy to Yahweh]

Jeremiah is using the phrase **the nose and the heat** as a common expression of the culture to mean that Yahweh is very angry. Alternate translation: [wrath] See how you translated the similar phrase in 7:20.

9.note: See how you translated this phrase in [Jeremiah 36:1](ta:36).

9.q: בַ⁠שָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠⁠חֲמִשִׁית לִ⁠יהוֹיָקִ֨ים בֶּן־יֹאשִׁיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ בַּ⁠חֹ֣דֶשׁ הַ⁠תְּשִׁעִ֔י
9.note: This is the ninth month of the Hebrew calendar. It is during the last part of November and the first part of December on Western calendars. “after Jehoiakim son of Josiah had been king of Judah for more than four years, during the ninth month”

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the presence of Yahweh]

Jeremiah is not distinguishing this **people** from another people that did not come to Jerusalem from the cities of Judah. Jeremiah is reminding the audience that all the people who had traveled to Jerusalem from the cities of Judah had come for the fast. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [and all the people, who had traveled to Jerusalem from the cities of Judah,]

10.note: The words **Gemariah** and **Shaphan** are the names of men.

11.note: The word **Micaiah** is the name of a man. See how you translated the names ** Gemariah** and **Shaphan** in the previous verse.

12.note: Jeremiah is introducing **all the officials**, whose names he lists in the rest of the verse, as new participants in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [there sat all the officials]

12.q: אֱלִישָׁמָ֣ע הַ⁠סֹּפֵ֡ר וּ⁠דְלָיָ֣הוּ בֶן־שְׁ֠מַעְיָהוּ וְ⁠אֶלְנָתָ֨ן בֶּן־עַכְבּ֜וֹר וּ⁠גְמַרְיָ֧הוּ בֶן־שָׁפָ֛ן וְ⁠צִדְקִיָּ֥הוּ בֶן־חֲנַנְיָ֖הוּ
12.note: The words **Elishama**, **Delaiah**, **Elnathan**, **Akbor**, **Zedekiah** and **Hananiah** are the names of men. See how you translated the names **Gemariah** and **Shaphan** in the previous verse and see how you translated the name **Shemaiah** in 29:24.

13.note: See how you translated this man’s name in Jeremiah 36:11.
The word “them” refers to officials in the previous verse. Alternate translation: [to those officials]
See how you translated the similar clause in Jeremiah 2:2.

14.q: אֶת יְהוּדִ֡י בֶּן נְ֠תַנְיָהוּ בֶּן שֶׁלֶמְיָ֣הוּ בֶן כּוּשִׁי֮
14.note: The words **Jehudi**, **Nethaniah**, **Shelemiah**, and **Cushi** are the names of men.

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what the officials wanted Baruch to do before the information about which scroll they meant. Alternate translation: [Take in your hand the scroll that you read in the ears of the people, and go]

15.note: See how you translated the similar phrase in Jeremiah 2:2.

16.note: Jeremiah is using **they expressed dread, a man to his neighbor** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they turned to one another in fear.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that they looked at one another in fear]

16.q: הַגֵּ֤יד נַגִּיד֙ לַ⁠מֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַ⁠דְּבָרִ֖ים & הָ⁠אֵֽלֶּה
16.note: The officials are repeating forms of the verb **report** in order to intensify their expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [We must indeed report all these words to the king]

17.note: See how you translated the similar expression in Jeremiah 36:4. Alternate translation: [Did Jeremiah dictate these messages to you?]

18.q: מִ⁠פִּי⁠ו֙ יִקְרָ֣א אֵלַ֔⁠י אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַ⁠דְּבָרִ֖ים הָ⁠אֵ֑לֶּה
18.note: See how you translated the phrase “From his mouth” in the previous verse. Alternate translation: [Jeremiah dictated all these messages to me] or [Jeremiah spoke all these messages to me]

A **ink** is a kind of liquid used for writing. If your readers would not be familiar with what ink is, you could use the name of a similar substance that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [with a dark liquid used for writing]

19.note: The officials are using **a man** as a common expression of the culture to mean “anyone.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and let no one know where you are] or [and do not let anyone know where you are]

20.q: וַ⁠יָּבֹ֤אוּ אֶל הַ⁠מֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ חָצֵ֔רָ⁠ה וְ⁠אֶת הַ⁠מְּגִלָּ֣ה הִפְקִ֔דוּ בְּ⁠לִשְׁכַּ֖ת אֱלִישָׁמָ֣ע הַ⁠סֹּפֵ֑ר
20.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the officials leaving the scroll in the chamber of Elishama before the information about their going to the king, since the officials had already left the scroll there before they went to the king. Alternate translation: [And the scroll they deposited in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and then they went to the king, into the courtyard]
See how you translated the phrase “in the ears of” in 2:2. Alternate translation: [in the hearing of]

21.note: See how you translated this man’s name in Jeremiah 36:14.
See how you translated the phrase “in the ears of” in 2:2. Alternate translation: [and in the hearing of]

The author is not distinguishing **the officials** from **the ones standing beside the king**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make the relationship between these phrases clearer. Alternate translation: [the officials who stood beside the king]

22.q: וְ⁠הַ⁠מֶּ֗לֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב֙ בֵּ֣ית הַ⁠חֹ֔רֶף בַּ⁠חֹ֖דֶשׁ הַ⁠תְּשִׁיעִ֑י וְ⁠אֶת הָ⁠אָ֖ח לְ⁠פָנָ֥י⁠ו מְבֹעָֽרֶת
22.note: Jeremiah is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

The implication is that **the house of the winter** was the part of the king’s palace where he lived during the cold season because it was warmer. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in the warmer rooms of his palace that he used during the winter]
See how you translated “in the ninth month” in 36:9.

A **brazier** is a kind of metal container that holds burning coals to heat a room. If your readers would not be familiar with what a brazier is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. This also occurs in verse 23. Alternate translation: [the coal heater]

Here, **face** represents the front of the king. The phrase **to his face** means “in front of him.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before him]

23.note: The pronoun **he** refers to the king, not to Jehudi, who was reading the scroll. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [that the king would cut it up in pieces]

24.q: וְ⁠לֹ֣א פָחֲד֔וּ וְ⁠לֹ֥א קָרְע֖וּ אֶת בִּגְדֵי⁠הֶ֑ם הַ⁠מֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְ⁠כָל עֲבָדָ֔י⁠ו הַ⁠שֹּׁ֣מְעִ֔ים אֵ֥ת כָּל הַ⁠דְּבָרִ֖ים הָ⁠אֵֽלֶּה
24.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about who these people were, **the king and all his servants, the ones hearing all these words**, before the information about what they did not do. Alternate translation: [And the king and all his servants, the ones hearing all these words, were not afraid, and they did not tear their garments]

Tearing one’s garments was a symbolic action by which people showed great sorrow and/or repentance. By saying that the king and his servants **did not tear their garments**, Jeremiah shows that they were not sorry and did not repent when they heard Yahweh’s words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and they did not tear their garments as a sign of grief and repentance]

24.q: הַ⁠מֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְ⁠כָל־עֲבָדָ֔י⁠ו הַ⁠שֹּׁ֣מְעִ֔ים אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַ⁠דְּבָרִ֖ים הָ⁠אֵֽלֶּה
24.note: The author is not distinguishing **the king and all his servants** from **the ones hearing**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make the relationship between these phrases clearer. Alternate translation: [the king and all his servants who heard all these words]

25.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 26:5. This also occurs in verse 31.
See how you translated the names of these men in 36:25.

26.q: אֶת יְרַחְמְאֵ֨ל בֶּן הַ⁠מֶּ֜לֶךְ וְ⁠אֶת שְׂרָיָ֣הוּ בֶן עַזְרִיאֵ֗ל וְ⁠אֶת שֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּֽן עַבְדְּאֵ֔ל
26.note: The words **Jerahmeel**, **Seraiah**, **Azriel**, **Shelemiah**, and **Abdeel** are the names of men.

27.note: See how you translated this expression in 28:12.
See how you translated the phrase “from the mouth of Jeremiah” in 36:4. Alternate translation: [at the dictation of Jeremiah]

27.q: אֶת־הַ⁠מְּגִלָּה֙ וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠דְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּתַ֥ב בָּר֛וּךְ מִ⁠פִּ֥י יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ
27.note: Jeremiah is not distinguishing this **scroll** from another scroll that is not the one containing the words that Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah. Jeremiah is reminding the reader which scroll the king burned, so that the reader understands it was the one on which Baruch had written down everything Jeremiah had dictated to him. Alternate translation: [the scroll that contained the words that Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah]

29.q: כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אַ֠תָּה שָׂרַ֜פְתָּ אֶת הַ⁠מְּגִלָּ֤ה הַ⁠זֹּאת֙ לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר מַדּוּעַ֩ כָּתַ֨בְתָּ עָלֶ֜י⁠הָ לֵ⁠אמֹ֗ר בֹּֽא יָב֤וֹא מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֙ וְ⁠הִשְׁחִית֙ אֶת הָ⁠אָ֣רֶץ הַ⁠זֹּ֔את וְ⁠הִשְׁבִּ֥ית מִמֶּ֖⁠נָּה אָדָ֥ם וּ⁠בְהֵמָֽה
29.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh says that you yourself have burned this scroll, asking why Jeremiah wrote on it that the king of Babylon would certainly come and destroy this land and cause man and beast to cease from it]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **You** separately, even though the verb translated as **you have burned** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that Jehoiakim himself, and no one else, burned the scroll. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [It is you who burned this scroll]

Yahweh is quoting Jehoiakim using the question form to rebuke Jeremiah for writing this message on the scroll, not to ask Jeremiah for information. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not have written on it]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **come** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [the king of Babylon will certainly come]

30.note: The term translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before, which is that Jehoiakim burned the scroll. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [Because of what Jehoiakim did]

30.q: לֹא יִֽהְיֶה לּ֥⁠וֹ יוֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֑ד
30.note: Here, **one sitting on the throne of David** represents “someone ruling as king over the kingdom of David.” Yahweh means that none of Jehoiakim’s descendants will rule as king. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [There will not be anyone from his family who rules as king over the kingdom of David]

30.q: וְ⁠נִבְלָת⁠וֹ֙ תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה מֻשְׁלֶ֔כֶת לַ⁠חֹ֥רֶב בַּ⁠יּ֖וֹם וְ⁠לַ⁠קֶּ֥רַח בַּ⁠לָּֽיְלָה
30.note: Yahweh is referring to all of the time and to every kind of weather by naming two major components, **the heat by the day** and **the frost by the night**. He means that Jehoiakim’s body will lie unburied and exposed at all times. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and his dead body will be thrown out to lie exposed to every kind of weather at all times]

The expression **will be thrown** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and others will throw his dead body]

31.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if Jehoiakim’s descendants were his **seed**. See how you translated “seed” in 7:15 where it is used with the same meaning. Alternate translation: [his offspring]
See how you translated the similar expression in 4:3.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **calamity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all the terrible things that I have said would happen to them] or [all the disastrous things that I have said would happen to them]

32.note: The expression **were added** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The context indicates that Jeremiah spoke these additional words and Baruch wrote them down. Alternate translation: [Jeremiah spoke many words like them, and Baruch added them to the scroll]
See how you translated the phrase “from the mouth of Jeremiah” in 36:4. Alternate translation: [at the dictation of Jeremiah]
